relatedSnapshot.title: Paid done-for-you inbox orders stay on "waiting for payment" when the user doesn't return from checkout
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a user pays for done-for-you domains and inboxes but doesn't land back on our page after checkout, the order stays on "waiting for payment" even though the money has left their account. We want the app to notice the payment by itself, so paying users get their inboxes without contacting support and don't lose trust in the purchase.

## Problem

On 11 Oct 2026 the owner of the Company Thirteen workspace paid $99.32 at 5:19 pm Name 1 for 3 domains and 9 inboxes, and Autumn recorded the payment. The email accounts page still said "Your inbox order is waiting for payment". When he clicked "Complete payment" at 5:24 pm, he got "Something went wrong". If he'd clicked "Cancel order" instead, he could have cancelled an order he'd already paid for, which is what happened in ENG-14226. We marked his order paid by hand at 5:35 pm and it's now setting up.

## Root cause

Only the user's browser confirms a done-for-you order after checkout, so a closed tab or lost redirect leaves a paid order pending, and every button on the pending card then does the wrong thing.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Today
    A[User pays in Autumn checkout] --> B{Browser returns to our page?}
    B -- yes --> C[confirmDfyOrder marks paid, setup starts]
    B -- no --> D[Order stays waiting for payment]
    D --> E[Complete payment: new checkout with same subscription IDs]
    E --> F[Autumn rejects: already in use. User sees Something went wrong]
    D --> G[Cleanup job after 30 min: cancels it without checking payment]
    G --> H[Reconcile job: can bring it back, but only on its own schedule and without renewal prices]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[User pays in Autumn checkout] --> B2{Browser returns?}
    B2 -- yes --> C2[confirmDfyOrder, unchanged]
    B2 -- no --> D2[Order waiting for payment]
    D2 --> E2[Complete payment or Cancel order: check this order's own Autumn subscriptions]
    D2 --> G2[Cleanup job: checks this order's subscriptions before cancelling]
    E2 -- all active --> P[Mark paid once, set renewal prices, start setup]
    G2 -- all active --> P
    E2 -- none --> K[Open checkout or cancel, as today]
  end
```

The check uses the order's own Autumn subscriptions, not the account's overall balance, because leftover balance from an earlier failed order could otherwise make an unpaid order look paid.

## Who's affected

In the last 30 days, 42 Autumn done-for-you orders completed and 1 got stuck like this (the Company Thirteen order), counted from the read-only production replica on 11 Oct 2026. We don't know how many past orders the cron confirmed without setting renewal prices, because nothing records which path confirmed an order. That count is a follow-up.

## Proposed fix

* Add a reader that checks a done-for-you order's own Autumn subscriptions: one per domain, plus one inbox subscription per domain that has inboxes. It says whether they're all active and not past due.
* Use it in "Complete payment", "Cancel order", the 30-minute cleanup job and the reconcile job. When the order is paid, mark it paid once (guarded so only one caller wins), set the renewal prices and start setup.
* When Autumn can't be read or the subscriptions are only partly there, don't cancel and don't confirm. Show a clear message instead of "Something went wrong".
* Stop `confirmDfyOrder` from re-sending setup for an order that's already setting up, so we can't place a second supplier order.

## Out of scope

* Pre-warmed orders: ENG-14227 owns them.
* A guard against duplicate starts inside the supplier setup job, and repairing renewal prices on past orders. Both are follow-ups.

## Done when

* "Complete payment" on a paid done-for-you order marks it paid and starts setup, opens no new checkout, and shows "Payment received. Setting up your inboxes."
* "Cancel order" on a paid done-for-you order doesn't cancel it.
* The cleanup job doesn't cancel a paid done-for-you order, and still cancels one with no Autumn subscriptions.
* An order whose only "proof" is leftover account balance from another order is never marked paid.
* Two callers confirming the same order at once start setup once.
* Regression tests cover each of these at the confirm, checkout and cleanup seams.

## Implementation context

* Code at dcb9d1b1a4: `createDfyCheckout`, `confirmDfyOrder` and `cancelDomainPurchaseOrder` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts`, `cleanup-stale-orders-cron.ts` and `reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts` in `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/`, and the pending card in `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/domain-provisioning-status.tsx`.
* Evidence: Sentry ACQUISITY-3XD for the "already in use" checkout error.
* The full plan and the review of it are in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed paid state is written only by a client confirmation call and the reconcile lane ignores orders under an hour: a captured payment can leave the workspace unprovisioned in pending_payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A pre-warmed domain/inbox order's paid state is written only by a client-side confirmation call; there is no provider-side signal for Autumn-billed pre-warmed checkouts. When that call does not complete, the customer's money is captured, the domain and inbox entitlements sit live and unused in billing, and the workspace keeps showing the order as "waiting for payment" with nothing provisioned and no way for anyone to move it.

## Problem

The customer pays, sees an empty mailbox list, and is told the order is still waiting for payment. Nothing in the product or in an admin tool can confirm or provision it. The only recovery is a scheduled pass that cannot select an order younger than an hour, and its newest-order-per-account gate can push a paid order out of that lane entirely. If no pass reaches the order within 24 hours the stale-order cron cancels it, so the customer waits up to a day for items they have already paid for.

## Root cause

A pre-warmed order's paid state is written in exactly two places, and this defect bypasses both:

* `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts` `confirmDomainPurchase` (line 2541), reached only from client code: `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/buy-all/checkout-view.tsx` (`proceedWithCheckout` -> `handlePaymentSuccess`, the leg used when `createMultiAttachCheckout` returns no payment URL under `redirect_mode: 'if_required'`), `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/checkout-return-handler.tsx` (`handleCheckoutReturn`), and `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/domain-provisioning-status.tsx` (`handleCompletePayment` on the pending-order card).
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, step `find-pending-orders-to-check`, which selects pending_payment orders only with `lt(createdAt, oneHourAgo)` and only for the newest actionable order per organization and billing account (`find-latest-actionable-orders-per-billing-account`).

No file under `apps/web/app/api/webhooks` writes a domain purchase order for Autumn-billed orders; `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/autumn/route.ts` handles products-updated and lapse events only, and the Whop partner webhook is the only provider-side writer, covering partner organizations. Verified at commit 4845e5940e1eb56662b687e98f54ed92a1de45de.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected: 1 workspace, 1 user — one captured charge, 9 domains and 27 inboxes provisioned = 0, with the entitlements live and unused in billing. Counted 2026-09-24.

Potentially exposed, counted 2026-09-24: a production-side proxy for orders whose client confirmation did not land is a paid pre-warmed Autumn order whose `paid_at` falls within 10 minutes after `last_payment_check_at` (the reconcile pass confirmed it, not the client leg) — 76 of 843 paid pre-warmed Autumn orders created in the previous 90 days, including repeat orders from the affected workspace, counted with `select count(*) filter (where paid_at is not null and last_payment_check_at is not null and paid_at >= last_payment_check_at and paid_at <= last_payment_check_at + interval '10 minutes') from domain_purchase_order where order_type='pre_warmed' and billing_account_id is not null and created_at > now() - interval '90 days'`. The proxy over-counts (a cron-checked paid order may also have been client-confirmed earlier) and cannot be split into "would have provisioned anyway" versus "saved only by the cron" without per-order provider reads, so exposure sits at or below 76.

Separately, pending_payment pre-warmed Autumn orders created in the last 7 days: 1 order / 1 organization, none older than an hour at count time; 2 pre-warmed orders were refunded by the reservation-expired lane in the same window.

## Proposed fix

A captured payment must end in a written paid state and provisioning, or in a refund, without depending on a client response: record the paid state from a provider-side signal for Autumn-billed pre-warmed orders, and close the blind window so an unpaid-looking order that has been paid is detected in minutes rather than after the hourly gate. Keep the newest-order-per-account gate from hiding an older paid order, and surface a state that separates "paid but not yet confirmed" from "abandoned", so support can act instead of guessing.

## What's included

In scope: the paid-state write path for pre-warmed Autumn orders, its provider-side signal, and the pending-payment selection window and ordering gate in the reconcile pass. Not in scope: the Whop partner path (it already records paid orders from its own webhook), the reservation-cancelled reactivation lane owned by ENG-14199, and the mail provider pipeline, which is never reached for these orders.

Worth owning separately, per the incident assessment for the triggering report:

* Customer recovery: provision an affected paid order or refund it when its reservations have lapsed — a human decision per workspace.
* Observability: no signal today distinguishes a paid-but-unconfirmed order from an abandoned one; the affected order was invisible until a customer reported it.
* Containment: the customer-facing "Complete payment" control on the pending-order card re-runs the checkout against already-attached subscriptions; its double-charge safety is unassessed, so it should not be advised until Autumn idempotency is confirmed.

## Regression seam

Boundary: the pending-payment confirmation of an Autumn-billed pre-warmed order. Trigger: a checkout whose subscription attach succeeds and settles payment while the client confirmation call never returns a paid state. Observable red before the fix: the order stays pending_payment with `paid_at` NULL and `last_payment_check_at` NULL, zero provisioned items, and no lane selecting it for at least an hour. Green after: the paid state is recorded from a server-side signal within minutes and provisioning starts, or the order is refunded with its reservations released.

## Done when

* A pre-warmed Autumn checkout whose payment is captured but whose client confirmation does not land is confirmed and provisioned, or refunded, without waiting for a customer report.
* A paid order cannot be excluded from recovery because it is less than an hour old or because a newer order exists on the same account.
* A regression test proves the causal mechanism at the pending-payment confirmation seam named above.
* The exposed population is re-counted after deployment and reported.

## Reports

* ENG-14226

relatedSnapshot.title: Paid DFY order for 3 domains and 9 inboxes stuck in "provisioning" for 13 days: the provisioning run stopped mid-poll and the state has no recovery path
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Testable claim

A workspace's paid Done-For-You (DFY) order for 3 domains and 9 inboxes is still in `provisioning` with 0 domains and 0 inboxes provisioned 13 days after payment, instead of the inboxes being set up within hours. The order's provisioning run stopped progressing after its first poll and the `provisioning` state has no recovery path.

## Intercom source

<url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context (bounded, sufficient to resume without the Slack transcript):

* Customer reports, with a screenshot, that the inboxes paid for on Sept 5 (local) are still provisioning; asked to confirm the signup email and created domains; a later screenshot supplies the email.
* Support (Name 6 Name 7) has already told the customer it is under investigation. No reply has been sent from this investigation.

## Evidence

**Production (PlanetScale, read 2026-09-17)**

* One DFY order: `order_type = dfy`, `domain_count = 3`, `inbox_count_per_domain = 0`, `provider = coldmailreseller`, created 2026-09-04T18:09:58Z, paid 2026-09-04T18:10:09Z, `provisioning_started_at` 2026-09-04T18:10:12Z, status `provisioning`, `domains_provisioned = 0`, `inboxes_provisioned = 0`, `error = NULL`, `completed_at = NULL`.
* `dfy_config.coldMailOrderId` IS set (provider order created and saved), so this is not the "failed before the provider order id was saved" variant.
* 3 `mail_domain` rows (all owned by the reporting organization, none claimed by another organization) stuck `pending`, `expected_inboxes = 3` each, `provisioned_at = NULL`, no error.
* 9 `mail_inbox` rows stuck `pending`, `connected = false`, `provider_id = NULL`, `retry_count = 0`.

**Name 8 (Inngest)**

* Exactly one run exists for this order: function `ai-clients.coldmailreseller.create-order`, run `01M1PST8C0BQQZK7S2QWPFD3CF`, queued 2026-09-04T18:10:09Z, status still RUNNING on 2026-09-17.
* Its trace completes `fetch-order` → `update-status-provisioning` → `resolve-order-domain-payment-linkage` → `sync-mail-records-pending` → `create-coldmail-order` → `save-coldmail-order-id` → `check-status-0-0` → `wait-0-0` (sleep, ended 2026-09-04T18:15:32Z). No step runs after that for 13 days: the poll loop never resumes and `update-order-complete` is never reached.
* Four sibling DFY orders picked at random in the same month (Aug 29, Aug 31, Sep 8, Sep 10) show the other variant: their runs FAILED at `sync-mail-records-pending` and were left in `provisioning` as well.

**Code**

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` · `processCreateColdMailOrder`: the order is set to `provisioning` up front (line \~164); the only path that writes a terminal status is `update-order-complete` (line \~789) after the whole per-domain polling loop. A run that stops mid-loop leaves the order non-terminal forever.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts` · `find-stuck-paid-orders`: recovery only selects `status = 'paid'` AND `provisioning_started_at IS NULL` (lines \~438-445). `find-orders-requiring-attention` only selects `requires_attention`. A stalled `provisioning` order matches neither.
* `apps/web/lib/billing/order-finalization.ts` · `deferDfyProviderOrderFailureToReconcile`: moves a stuck DFY order to `requires_attention`, but only from the function's `onFailure`, i.e. only when the run actually fails. A run that never fails never triggers it.
* UI: `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/domain-provisioning-status.tsx` renders "Provisioning domains (0/3)..." for this status with no cancel, dismiss or retry action, and `getInboxOrderReadiness` treats `provisioning` as an in-flight order.

**Blast radius (current query, 2026-09-17)**

* 10 orders across 10 distinct organizations are in `provisioning` more than 24 hours after provisioning started (oldest 2026-01-04, newest 2026-09-10); 13 orders across 13 organizations are in `provisioning` in total, of which 6 started in September.

## Lanes not run

* Screenshots in the conversation were routed for image reading and could not be returned; they are corroborating only and the verdict does not depend on them.
* Provider-side (ColdMailReseller) mailbox state has no read tool in this workflow.

## Unblock

No customer self-service action exists: the order is non-terminal, the card offers no cancel/dismiss/retry, and re-triggering the create-order event would create a duplicate provider order. A human must recover the stuck order (or refund it) from the workspace side; the durable fix belongs to the stuck-order recovery path.

relatedSnapshot.title: DFY orders paid for domains but not inboxes are cancelled as unpaid and never recovered or refunded
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a Done-For-You checkout charges for the domains but not the inboxes, our payment check never treats the order as paid. The order gets cancelled 30 minutes later as a payment timeout and is never recovered, refunded, or flagged for a person. The customer pays and receives nothing, and nobody here finds out unless they write in.

## Problem

The customer completes checkout and their card is charged for the domains, but no domains or inboxes ever appear. The order shows as cancelled with "Payment timeout - order automatically cancelled after 30 minutes", even though payment landed a few minutes after the order was created. Support only learns about it from the customer, days later.

## Root cause

There are two parts, and only the second is proven.

1. The trigger is not settled. `createDfyCheckout` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts` asks Autumn's multiAttach for one Inbox (DFY) plan per domain, with the quantity set to that domain's mailbox count, and the production catalog mapping for the `inbox_dfy` slot is correct. In the affected order, though, the Inbox (DFY) plans were recorded at quantity 0, and the Stripe invoice carries only the domain lines. Why that happened couldn't be established because the request logs weren't available (Axiom and Sentry). Whoever owns Autumn checkout needs to look at the multiAttach request and response.
2. The recovery gap is proven. `getDomainOrderPaymentStatus` in `apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/client.ts` only treats an order as paid when the domain balance and the inbox balance are both high enough. With the inbox balance at 0:
   * the confirm path never marks the order paid;
   * `billing.cleanup-stale-orders-cron` (`cleanup-stale-orders-cron.ts`) cancels it after 30 minutes without checking the provider;
   * the cancelled-order reactivation lane in `billing.reconcile-domain-orders-cron` (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, `check-cancelled-payment-<id>`) re-checks with the same both-wallets rule for 24 hours and then drops the order for good.

   No lane flags or refunds an order whose domains were paid and whose inboxes weren't.

## Blast radius

1 org and 1 user confirmed stranded. There are 7 Autumn-billed DFY orders cancelled as payment timeouts in the 60 days to 13 Oct 2026, across 4 orgs. The other 6 orders (3 orgs) were each followed by a successful order in the same org, so they look like retried checkouts, but they haven't been checked against Autumn for zero-quantity inbox plans. Query: `domain_purchase_order` where order_type = 'dfy', billing provider = autumn, error like 'Payment timeout%', created in the last 60 days, compared against later completed, paid, provisioning or requires_attention orders in the same org. Counted 13 Oct 2026. Other DFY orders from 4 to 6 Oct were marked paid within seconds, so checkout isn't broadly down.

## Proposed fix

A DFY checkout should bill every inbox it asks for, or fail loudly before the customer pays. Separately, when the provider shows any payment against an order that our check still treats as unpaid, the order shouldn't be silently cancelled. It should be flagged for a person, or have the partial payment refunded automatically, and that has to hold in both the cleanup and reconcile lanes.

## What's included

* Finding why the multiAttach inbox quantities ended up at 0.
* Handling partially paid orders in `cleanup-stale-orders-cron` and in the reconcile reactivation lane.
* DFY and pre-warmed orders both. The pending-lane timing gap in ENG-14227 (reconcile ignores orders under an hour while cleanup cancels at 30 minutes) is the same seam, so coordinate with it.
* Out of scope: per-customer billing remediation, which stays on the report tickets.

## Regression seam

Take a DFY order whose billing customer has domain balance >= domain_count and inbox balance < its mailbox count, with created_at more than 30 minutes ago. Today the cleanup cron sets it to cancelled with the payment-timeout error and reconcile never reactivates it (red). After the fix, it ends up flagged for attention or refunded instead (green).

## Done when

* A DFY checkout's invoice includes the inbox lines for every mailbox in `dfy_config`, or checkout fails before payment.
* An order with partial provider payment is never cancelled as a payment timeout without being refunded or flagged for a person.
* A regression test proves the partial-payment case at the cleanup and reconcile seam.

## Reports

* ENG-15299

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: unpaid mailboxes from a refunded DFY order cannot be paid from the billing page
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The billing page cannot take payment for mailboxes that the platform still bills the provider for. When a Done-For-You domain order is refunded because the provider failed to provision it, the mailboxes it created are still live and in use, the audit flags them unpaid and warns they will be cancelled on a dated deadline, and the resubscribe control that would settle them never renders. Customers see a warning they cannot act on, and the mailboxes are removed while they are willing to pay.

## Problem

An owner opens Settings -> Billing from the "Review billing" banner, expecting to pay for the mailboxes the banner names. The page shows no managed domains for that workspace, so there is no "Review and resubscribe" and no per-domain "Resubscribe", and no other surface opens the pay dialog. Support then tells the customer a payment failed, when the only inbox charge was refunded.

## Root cause

`apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` `listManagedDomains` inner-joins the domain's purchase order and filters `ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded')` (and `ne(mailDomainTable.status, 'suspended')`). A refunded order therefore removes its domain from the managed list even while an open unpaid audit finding exists for it. `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` `EmailAccountsDomainsCard` returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" buttons, and those are the only entry points to the pay flow (`apps/web/trpc/routers/cmr-domain-charges.ts` `listUnpaid` already returns the domain for an owner or admin, regardless of order status). When the card does render for a workspace with other domains, the refunded domain is still hidden from the list, so its per-domain control is missing too.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-10-05 against production. 4 organizations and 9 open `unpaid` findings belong to a refunded purchase order; 2 of those organizations have an empty managed list, where the control is unreachable (6 findings), and the other 2 keep 3 and 4 visible managed domains, where only the per-domain control is missing (3 findings). All 4 organizations have a sent unpaid reminder dated 2026-09-29, so all 4 face a 2026-10-06 cancellation date. Distinct affected users were not counted: the audit rows carry no user id.

```
WITH f AS (SELECT fa.organization_id FROM cmr_domain_audit_finding fa
  JOIN domain_purchase_order o ON o.id = fa.order_id
  WHERE fa.payment_state = 'unpaid' AND fa.resolved_at IS NULL
    AND fa.dismissed_at IS NULL AND o.status = 'refunded')
SELECT f.organization_id::text, count(*) AS open_findings,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM mail_domain md
     JOIN domain_purchase_order o2 ON o2.id = md.order_id
    WHERE md.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND md.status <> 'suspended' AND o2.status <> 'refunded') AS visible_managed_domains,
  (SELECT min(r.created_at)::text FROM cmr_renewal_reminder r
    WHERE r.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND r.kind = 'unpaid' AND r.status = 'sent') AS first_sent_reminder
FROM f GROUP BY f.organization_id
```

Confirmed affected: 2 organizations with the control unreachable. Potentially exposed: the further 2 organizations whose refunded domain is hidden from the list while their pay-all control is reachable.

## Proposed fix

Make the unpaid-mailbox notice actionable for every workspace that carries an open unpaid finding. A workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are still live should be able to pay for them from the billing page: the pay control should be reachable from the unpaid findings themselves rather than only from the managed domain list, and a refunded order's domain should stay visible to the billing card while an open unpaid finding exists so its per-domain "Resubscribe" renders as well. The customer-facing outcome is that the banner's deadline can be met from the billing page, without an operator making a production or billing change by hand.

## What's included

Both variants found in the blast radius (empty card, and refunded domain hidden beside visible ones). Not included: the upstream provisioning failure that leaves mailboxes live after a refunded order (owned by the DFY provisioning family tracked under ENG-13213), and the wording of the reminder emails. Related umbrella work: ENG-13358, whose child ENG-14423 covers giving customers a clear date to act by. Separately filed work needed for the current cohort: an operator must make the affected mailboxes payable, or decide they are removed, before 2026-10-06.

## Regression seam

The billing page's managed-domain list and its pay control. Red before: for a workspace whose only mail domain belongs to a refunded order while an open unpaid finding exists, `listManagedDomains` returns nothing and the billing card renders its empty state with no pay control. Green after: the same workspace offers a working resubscribe path that charges for the live mailboxes and clears the finding.

## Done when

* An owner of a workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are live can open Settings -> Billing and pay for those mailboxes from the page.
* A workspace that also has other managed domains shows the per-domain resubscribe control for the refunded domain while its unpaid finding is open.
* A regression test at the list/pay seam proves both cases red before and green after.

## Reports

* ENG-14710 (customer report, Company Four workspace; carries the full investigation document).

## Testable claim

In the reported workspace, Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains lists 6 domains and 18 inboxes while Cold Email Agent -> Email Accounts lists only 6 inboxes, because four of the six Done-For-You domains (12 inboxes) failed provider provisioning and are still held in a requires_attention order, un-cancellable and still billed.

## Intercom conversation context

Reporter states (2026-09-10): the Billing settings show 6 domains with 3 emails each, but the campaign Email Accounts tab only shows 6. She expected 18, says office hours confirmed a bug, and shared screenshots. A campaign page also showed "No email accounts connected. Add one to start sending." on an Active campaign.
Conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Evidence

* Production: domain_purchase_order status requires_attention, completedAt null; 6 mail_domain rows in status failed ("Domain or mailbox provisioning failed"), provisionedAt null; 12 mail_inbox rows status error, connected false, retryCount 0, lastRetryAt null; 6 mail_inbox rows active/connected. Order created 2026-08-16.
* Name 8: billing.reconcile-domain-orders-cron runs every 30 minutes and still re-attempts the same unconnected inboxes; mail_inbox.retryCount never advances.
* Provider: Company Seven account list for the workspace returns exactly 6 active accounts, matching the 6 provisioned inboxes.
* Help center: the Billing card is a domain/inbox billing view and is explicitly not a provisioning status panel, so the count difference itself is expected; the defect is the unresolved failed domains.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-09-10)

* 7 requires_attention orders across 6 organizations hold 22 failed domains.
* 33 unconnected, never-retried inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days, across 5 organizations.

## Suggested link

Overlaps the existing DFY failed-domain master family (failed domains left claimed, un-cancellable and still billed); dedupe and parent during routing.

## Customer report

```text
This is a billing dispute for the billing team to reconcile. It is not a refund request yet, and nothing has been promised to the customer.

What the customer reports: Their campaign shows 15 inboxes, but 3 inboxes under <domain> are not in the campaign. Their Billing screen shows those inboxes in Error, with a payment due today (screenshot reading: "Normal · Error · Added September 14, 2026"). They say they have no idea what is going on, and they asked for a human agent. Support already had them check the Email Accounts page: all 15 listed inboxes are Active with 100% health, so the connected ones are fine. The customer did not say which charge they dispute beyond the inboxes now showing payment due.

What the results show:
- One done-for-you order, created 2026-09-14, records a paid date of 2026-09-14 20:56. Its status is requires_attention and it stopped at step 5/6. It reconciles to 6 domains and 18 inboxes charged, but 5 domains and 15 inboxes provisioned and connected. 1 domain failed and 3 inboxes are missing. A provisioning failure was recorded on 2026-09-28 with the message "Provisioned 5/6 domains, 15/18 inboxes". The order's technical error details are unavailable. No retry attempts are recorded (provisioningAttempts 0).
- The 6 domains in the order are <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain> and <domain>. I could not confirm from the results which of the six failed. The customer's screenshot and the earlier team notes point to <domain>.
- A paid invoice on 2026-09-14 for $198.26 (charge succeeded) lists 6 yearly domain lines ($11.46, $16.74, $14.29, $16.74, $14.29, $16.74) and inbox lines at $18.00 per month for 3 inboxes each, covering 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-14. The invoice lines are truncated, so I only saw 4 of the 6 inbox lines. No source ties this charge to the order, so payment for the order itself is unconfirmed. The invoice and the order both show 6 domains.
- Billing shows an active subscription for every one of the 6 domains and all 6 inbox groups, including <domain> inboxes, even though 3 inboxes on this order were not provisioned. The inbox allowance shows 18 granted, 15 used, 3 unused. The domain allowance shows 6 granted, 5 used, 1 unused.
- The inbox billing period from the 2026-09-14 invoice ended on 2026-10-14, which matches the customer seeing payment due today. The next inbox renewal, including the 3 undelivered inboxes, has not been confirmed as charged.
- The reconciliation note says Stripe shows a succeeded charge but the product database has no active subscription status for the organization. It should be checked for charged-but-not-provisioned.
- No refunds are recorded and there are no failed payments. The other recent charges are the Pro plan ($185 on 2026-09-14 and on 2026-10-14) and 50,000 credits ($300 on 2026-09-15). The customer has not disputed these.

What billing needs to do: reconcile what the customer was charged against what was delivered. Decide how to treat the missing domain and 3 inboxes, and whether the renewal due today should be charged for inboxes that were never set up. Also check whether provisioning for the failed domain should be re-run. The customer must not be asked to place a new order or pay again while this is unresolved.
```

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Intercom conversation

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Conversation context

Same Intercom thread as ENG-14509. On 2026-10-05 the customer (owner of the Company Four workspace) wrote: "The profile says review billing, and when we go in everything is in order, how do we resume the campaign?" Support answered that the campaign was active and not paused, then said "It seems that your payment for the inboxes did not go through. Kindly revisit your payment." Asked to check the Company Four workspace specifically, the customer replied "The payment date is only the 10th?" and, after support confirmed, asked: "Then how would the inbox payment not have gone through?"

## Testable claim

In the Company Four workspace, the 3 mailboxes on <domain> are flagged unpaid with a 6 October cancellation date, but the billing page lists no managed domains for that workspace, so the owner has no resubscribe control to pay for them and cannot act on the notice.

## Evidence

* Production audit row for the workspace: domain <domain>, payment_state 'unpaid' and open (no resolved_at, no dismissed_at) since 2026-09-10, held_domains 1, held_inboxes 3, paid_domains 0, paid_inboxes 0, mail_domain_status 'failed', note "Inboxes unpaid (aggregate)".
* The same row's order_id is a DFY domain purchase order whose status is 'refunded' (refunded 2026-08-11 after the provider failed to provision it; refundableDomains 1, refundableInboxes 3, retriesExhausted true).
* The workspace's only mail_domain row is that domain, status 'failed'. The provider-side mailbox subscription is still ACTIVE with auto-renew and period end 2026-10-11, and the 3 mailboxes exist and are 'active' in the app, so the workspace keeps sending from them.
* listManagedDomains filters out mail domains whose purchase order status is 'refunded' (and whose domain status is 'suspended'), so the managed list for this workspace is empty. EmailAccountsDomainsCard returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" controls, which are the only entry points to the pay-unpaid-mailboxes flow. The customer is an owner of the workspace, so the pay flow itself is available to her; it is simply unreachable from the page.
* Blast radius counted 2026-10-05: 4 organizations and 9 open 'unpaid' findings whose purchase order is refunded (query joined cmr_domain_audit_finding to domain_purchase_order on order_id, filtered payment_state 'unpaid', resolved_at and dismissed_at null, order status 'refunded').
* Two reminder emails for the unpaid mailboxes were sent on 2026-09-29 to <email> and <email>, which puts the notice's cancellation date at 2026-10-06 (7-day grace).
* The customer's report matches the code path: the billing page shows her nothing to pay.

## Code

* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts, listManagedDomains (the ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded') filter).
* apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx, EmailAccountsDomainsCard (empty-state early return hides the resubscribe controls).

## Customer report

```text
Billing dispute plus platform fault, for billing and Engineering to reconcile.

Customer (workspace owner, Name 13) reports that all inboxes used by the Company Ten campaign now show "not paid for". He says he never cancelled the inboxes, the campaign has stopped producing bookings, and his client is upset. He is asking how to get the domains and inboxes back. An earlier support message told him a ticket would be created.

What was found:
- Billing: the Pro subscription is active, $185/month. Pro-only charges succeeded on 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-29 and neither includes inboxes or domains. No October charge appears in the recent charges read; the current period runs to about 2026-10-29.
- The only inbox and domain charge is the 2026-07-29 subscription creation: 5 domains at $11.46/year plus 15 DFY inboxes at $18/month, total $147.30. That charge was fully refunded ($147.30). The matching second subscription is cancelled. Billing's own reconciliation flags a charge with no active subscription in the product database.
- Provisioning: the one DFY order (5 domains, 15 inboxes, created 2026-07-29) is saved as "refunded" and "cancelled", step 0/5, with a recorded error whose details are unavailable. It shows 5 domains charged and 5 failed, 0 domains active, 0 inboxes active, 15 inboxes missing, and a recorded provisioning start of 2026-07-29 17:29 UTC. Domains: <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>. Forwarding at purchase was to <domain>.
- Yet the live sending-account read shows all 15 inboxes on those 5 domains still exist, were created and started warmup on 2026-07-31 (the same day the order was marked completed/refunded), have never sent (no last-used date), and all 15 are currently in Error. Warmup score reads 100 on each. Connection to the sending provider is recorded as active with no connection error.
- Each inbox has one saved automatic reconnect retry, all between 2026-10-06 04:25 and 09:33 UTC, and all still not connected. The saved reason for each is a recorded diagnostic whose details are unavailable. The customer has no manual reconnect attempts on record.
- No other recent account errors, and no job failures were checked beyond this.

What is unconfirmed: why the inboxes went to Error. The saved error text could not be read, so cancellation for non-payment is a possibility but is not confirmed. It is also unconfirmed whether the inboxes were ever billed after the July refund, since the Aug and Sept invoices only list the Pro plan. The customer did not request a refund; he wants the inboxes working.

Needed: billing to reconcile the refunded July inbox and domain order against the 15 inboxes that were still provisioned and used for his campaign (and whether payment for them was ever properly collected), and Engineering to establish why all 15 went to Error around early October and whether they can be restored without a new purchase. Customer asks that the domains and inboxes be restored, and says the delay is costing him money and hurting his client relationship.
```

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer cannot buy more email inboxes: a DFY domain order stuck in provisioning hides Add New Inboxes and rejects new orders
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Testable claim

On 2026-08-18 a workspace owner paid for a Done-For-You domain order (1 domain, 3 mailboxes). The order has been stuck in `provisioning` with 0 of 1 domains provisioned ever since, so on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 the owner could not buy more email inboxes for SDRs: the "Provisioning domains" status churned with no progress and the platform refused the purchase ("Acquisity doesn't seem to want to accept my money"). Expected: buying more inboxes from Cold Email Agent → Email Accounts → Add New Inboxes.

## Intercom source

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Contact asked on 2026-09-21 for help because the "Provisioning domains" step had been churning with nothing happening while trying to buy more email inboxes. Fin AI answered with the normal provisioning-time answer and closed the conversation. The contact reopened it on 2026-09-22 saying it was the second day of trying and that Acquisity would not take the money, then said it was to buy more inboxes for SDRs. Fin AI offered human help; a teammate picked it up and asked whether the provisioning had been stuck for two days. No financial remedy was requested. Product area attribute set to Billing by an admin, then corrected to Email accounts & domains.

## Evidence summary

* Production: the organization's Done-For-You order is `provisioning`, paid 2026-08-18T22:10:12Z, provisioning_started_at 2026-08-18T22:10:14Z, updated_at unchanged since, domains_provisioned 0/1, inboxes_provisioned 0/3, provider_order_id null, error null, not dismissed, dfy_config has no coldMailOrderId.
* Production: the order's domain name is already claimed in `mail_domain` by a different organization as `failed` (created 2026-03-25).
* Code: `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` step `sync-mail-records-pending` inside `processCreateColdMailOrder` throws `Unable to claim domains for this organization: <domain>` at line 301 when the conflicting row belongs to another organization, because the upsert's `setWhere` only updates rows of the same organization. The throw happens before the `create-coldmail-order` and `save-coldmail-order-id` steps, so the order never gets a provider order id and never reaches a terminal status.
* Code: `deferDfyProviderOrderFailureToReconcile` in `apps/web/lib/billing/order-finalization.ts` only flips a DFY order to `requires_attention` when `dfy_config->>'coldMailOrderId'` is set, so the on-failure recovery is a no-op here.
* Code: `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts` recovers `paid` orders with null `provisioningStartedAt`, `failed` orders, `requires_attention` orders and cancelled orders with a confirmed payment. A `provisioning` order with `provisioningStartedAt` set and no completion matches no recovery path.
* Code: `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/email-accounts-table.tsx` line 275 treats `provisioning` as an active order and hides "Add New Inboxes" (line 1346); `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts` `createDomainPurchaseOrder` (and the DFY equivalent) also reject a new order with "You already have an order in progress. Please wait for it to complete."
* No recovery is reachable by the customer: the order is not dismissed and offers no cancel/dismiss/retry.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-09-23)

9 domain purchase orders are stuck in `provisioning` across 9 organizations and 9 users, all with `provider_order_id IS NULL` and stale beyond 24 hours; 6 of them are `order_type = 'dfy'` across 6 organizations.

## Help center expectation

`apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/email-accounts/buying-inboxes.mdx` and the pre-warmed inbox FAQ state provisioning normally takes a few minutes to about an hour and that "Add New Inboxes" is the entry point for buying. Both are contradicted by state that has not moved in 35 days.

## Reproduction

Not reproducible from the customer side by design; the block is server state plus a hidden button. Verified from production rows and code.

Investigation journal: Slack thread in the intake channel for this conversation.

relatedSnapshot.title: Mailbox billing dispute: $54 monthly inbox charge after five months without a collected payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source**: <url:app.intercom.com> (opened 2026-10-04, assigned to Ellaine Fuente; the customer asked for a human on 2026-10-05)

**Customer**: <email>, owner of workspace "Name 16's Workspace" (org <uuid>, billing account <uuid>, native Autumn).

**Ask**: why he has to pay monthly for the mailboxes/domains. He says he opened them in May, that this is the first time since May he has paid, and asks whether $54 will recur every month. Taxonomy bucket: overcharged. No refund was requested.

**Finding**: the charge is correct and the customer paid it himself. He holds 9 live inboxes (3 domains x 3, DFY, all active and connected) at $6 per inbox per month = $54 per month; the three domains are billed yearly at $15.16 each, paid on 2026-04-29 through 2027-04-29. He paid $99.48 on 2026-04-29 and $54.00 on 2026-05-31. From 2026-06-29 his card declined repeatedly with insufficient funds, nothing more was collected, and the domain+inbox subscription was canceled for payment_failed on 2026-07-13. The mailbox audit flagged the 9 mailboxes unpaid on 2026-09-10; a human sent the unpaid-mailbox reminder on 2026-09-29 naming $54.00 a month and a 6 October deadline; the customer paid $54.00 from his own billing page on 2026-10-05 (audit trail cmr_domain_charge.create, actor = his own user id; the $54.00 charge was captured at 08:39 after one insufficient-funds decline at 08:38). No double billing: the earlier $54.00 invoice (2026-06-29) and the $185.00 Pro invoice (2026-09-11) remain open on canceled subscriptions and cover earlier periods.

**Exposure**: $54.00 collected 2026-10-05 for the period 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-05, matching the 9 paid inboxes. Nothing in the evidence supports a refund or a credit. Two invoices remain collectible on canceled subscriptions: $54.00 (2026-06-29) and $185.00 (2026-09-11).

**Proposed human action**: support explains the pricing to the customer (mailboxes are $6 per inbox per month, domains are yearly) and, if he wants the recurring charge stopped, cancels the three inbox add-ons on the billing account; separately decide what to do with the two open invoices on canceled subscriptions and make sure the mailbox audit re-runs so the workspace stops reading as unpaid. This is a proposal, not a promise.

**Also noted**: in the conversation the assistant told him the October charge was the "first monthly billing cycle catching up" and that June-October were renewals "happening in the background". That does not match the records (April and May were paid, June onward failed).

Full readout and evidence in the Billing investigation document on this ticket.
